frequency_question: How often do expiring multi-decade transboundary water treaties successfully get replaced by a signed successor agreement before their expiration date?
membership_rule: Includes any formal bilateral water-sharing treaty with a fixed multi-decade duration that reached its expiration or formal renewal window within the modern era (post-1945). Excludes non-binding declarations and internal river basin compacts.

cases.name: 1944 US-Mexico Water Treaty Mexican-American renegotiations (Minute 319/323 series)
Indus Waters Treaty continuous operational renegotiations under permanent mechanisms
Soviet-era Central Asian water allocation protocols transitioning post-1991 (Nukus Declaration framework)
Senegal River Basin Development Organization (OMVS) charter renewals

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major structured cases named; represents the primary global reference set for multi-decade water treaty renewals.
known_gaps: Does not fully account for acute short-term political transitions disrupting scheduled bureaucratic timelines.
skeleton: Global transboundary water treaty renewals over 70 years across 5 major continental basins showing historical precedent for eventual replacement despite delays.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 major structured historical precedents identified where core framework continuity was maintained.
validity_reason: International water law norms and hydro-diplomacy frameworks evolve slowly over decades.
